cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: I Know the Procedure
cards.instruction: Perform investigative confidence while quietly using each response to discover what the questions, clues, and next steps should be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I'll investigate the missing raffle tin. Naturally, we begin with access. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cleaner has the only cupboard key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. As expected. Where does our keyholder go after cleaning?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception. But the tin never went in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we've eliminated that location. Confirm where you last saw it; I'll establish our next search area.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 adopts keyholder lead and A5 pretends the wrong location was an elimination, but the extra rank claim does not reduce B work or invite actual cooperation.

responseLogic.evidence: B4 tin never in cupboard undermines A1 assumed access path; A5 calling it elimination is character face-saving, not proof the original premise was valid.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies keyholder and B4 both answers whereabouts and corrects relevance.

heightening.evidence: B4 correction forces A5 to start from last sighting while presenting that as a planned next search area.

specificity.evidence: A1 missing raffle tin and B2 key establish the investigation premise; B4 clarifies its flaw.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 voluntary please and A3 rank claim are redundant; A5 two procedural labels can become a concrete shared search task.
